court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Mahadev Maruti Pawar And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Mahadev s/o Maruti Pawar, Kavita w/o Mahadev Pawar, Yogesh s/o Mahadev Pawar, Shailesh s/o Mahadev Pawar (husband, parents-in-law and brother-in-law)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra Through Police Inspector, Shevgaon Police Station, Sumati w/o Shailesh Pawar (informant)

facts_of_case: Respondent No.2 set law in motion alleging that after her marriage in 2011, everything was smooth until 2013. Subsequently, husband and in-laws commented and taunted her for not preparing good food, for not cleaning clothes properly, and on such count, she was beaten and kept starved.

legal_principles.principle: The exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is subject to legal requirements.
legal_principles.held: Bearing in mind legal requirements on the point of exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., we proceed to examine whether the applicants herein have at all made out a prima facie case for grant of relief and whether prosecution launched against them is indeed abuse of process of law or not.
cited_cases: Inder Mohan Goswami and Anr. Vs. State of Uttaranchal and Ors., (2007) 12 SCC 1
Mahendra K.C. Vs. State of Karnataka and Another, (2022) 2 Supreme Court Cases 129

legal_principles.principle: A prima facie case must be made out for grant of relief in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: whether the applicants herein have at all made out a prima facie case for grant of relief
